data.narrative: Completed Module 5 'Stakeholder Communication' learning about communication medium tradeoffs, translating technical details to business impact, writing stakeholder memo for security delay, identifying 31 jargon terms in flawed email and buried Black Friday risk, and rewriting email to stakeholder-friendly version with clear asks.

dimension_scores.observation: Identified 31 jargon terms in Marcus's email and found the buried Black Friday risk that was hidden in technical language
dimension_scores.evidence: flawed_email_analysis.md contains detailed jargon count and risk identification

dimension_scores.observation: Wrote stakeholder memo opening with business impact (3-week delay) not technical details, translated all technical terms to plain language
dimension_scores.evidence: security_delay_memo.md opens with business impact and uses coat check analogy for tokenization

dimension_scores.observation: Rewrote infrastructure migration email for VP of Engineering and Head of Product, translating 31 technical terms to business language and ending with specific asks
dimension_scores.evidence: infrastructure_migration_fixed.md replaces Kong/NGINX with traffic routing system, ends with 3 clear asks

dimension_scores.observation: Chose written memo format for scalability and referenceability, structured emails with clear sections (summary, what happened, what we're doing, risks, what we need)
dimension_scores.evidence: Both memos use logical structure with headings and bullet points

dimension_scores.observation: Both stakeholder communications end with specific asks - security memo asks for approval of date shift and Thursday meeting, infrastructure memo asks for 2 engineers for 8 weeks, roadmap alignment, and load test timing
dimension_scores.evidence: Both documents have clear calls to action with specific decisions requested

strengths: Chose written memo format with reasoning about scalability and referenceability
Wrote stakeholder communications opening with business impact not technical details
Identified all jargon in flawed email (31 terms) and buried Black Friday risk
Rewrote flawed email to stakeholder-friendly version with clear asks
data.recommendation: Continue practicing stakeholder communication in real-world scenarios - the muscle of leading with impact, translating everything, and ending with what you need applies to any difficult conversation with non-technical stakeholders
